To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the tunneling currents (I) through single molecular bridges (1,6 hexanethiolate) between two gold protrusions by repeated formation of a break junction in STM and have found the increase in the currents (I) caused by the conformational change from gauche rich to all trans conformations in the alkylene chain.

we observed the change in alkyl chain conformation (i.e. change from gauche to trans) of 1, 6 hexanedithioate sandwiched between Au electrodes and measured single molecular conductivities of various rotamers of 1,4 hexanedithioates sandwiched between Au(111) electrodes by repeated break junction method under UHV.

we have measured the tunneling currents (i s) through single molecular junctions of Au/hexadithiolate/AU under UHV, and have found that the increase in tunneling currents can mainly be attributed to the change in the conformation of alkylene chains from gauche to trans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for measuring the single molecular conductivity and the study of the single molecular conductivities by this new technique.
the study of the single molecular conductivities and the effects of Au S contacts by the STM break junction measurements under UHV.

the development of a novel method to measure the single molecular conductivity by repeated formation of a break junction between an atomically flat gold substrate and a gold STM-tip in ultrahigh vacuum, and with the study of the effects of the molecular conformational change and the binding sites of thio-lates on gold on the single molecular conductivity of 1, 6 hexanedithio-late.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single molecular conductivities of Au/hexanethiolate/Au molecular bridges were strongly affected by the binding sites of thioaltes to gold.

(1) the single molecular conductivities through 1,6-hexanedithiolates with all-trans conformations were 1 order of magnitude higher than those through gauche rich conformations, and (2) the single molecular conductivity through 1, 6-hexanediothiate with gauche rich conformations was not affected significantly by the change of Au S binding sites from the 3-fold hollow site (3-H site) to the 2-fold bridge site (2-B site).

the single molecular conductivities of the 1,6-hexanedithiolated Au junctions are determined by the number of gauche conformations, the number of rotamers, the number of Au S contacts and the binding site of thiolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the single molecular conductivity can be increased by increasing the number of gauche conformations in the alkylene chains of alkyl thiols.

the effect of the Au S contacts on the single molecular conductivities can be clearly observed by the repeated break junction method under ultrahigh-vacuum condition, and that the conformational change of the alkylene chain from the gauche rich to the trans conformation is the most dominant factor for the observed gradual increase in the single molecule currents during the stretching of the molecular junction.
the conformational change of alkylene chains in single molecular junctions can be controlled and studied by the repeated formation of breakjunctions between a substrate and a gold STM-tip under UHV.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conformational change of the alkylene chain in 1,6-hexanedithiol from the gauche rich conformation to all trans con formation results in one order of magni tude increase in the single molec ular conductivity.

the single molecular conductivities are strongly affected by the change in conformations in alkylene chains and that the effect is much larger than the effect of AuS binding sites on single molecular conductivies.
the effect of Au-S contact on single molecule conductance can be studied in a more reliable way by the use of rigid pi conjugated molecules with the conformational effects removed.
